01 • Project aim

Aim and objectives

Aim: To implement a 4-bit digital-to-analog converter using an R-2R resistor ladder and an op-amp output stage, then observe its analog output for different digital input combinations.

Components visible in the supplied diagram

  • Four digital inputs: D3, D2, D1, D0
  • R ladder resistors: 10 kΩ
  • 2R ladder resistors: 20 kΩ
  • Feedback resistor Rf = 10 kΩ
  • 741 op-amp
  • Op-amp supplies: +15 V and −15 V
  • Oscilloscope XSC1

Learning objectives

  • Understand binary-weighted contributions in an R-2R ladder.
  • Calculate the ideal analog output for a 4-bit input.
  • Verify the output staircase for changing digital codes.
  • Compare theory with simulation measurements.
4-bit resolution = 16 codes
02 • Theory and working

How an R-2R DAC works

An R-2R ladder uses only two resistor values: R and 2R. Each digital bit connects its ladder branch to a logic-high reference or ground. The ladder generates binary-weighted currents, and the op-amp converts the summed current into an output voltage.

For the shown inverting op-amp arrangement, with ideal op-amp operation, matching resistor ratios, and logic-high reference voltage VH:

Vout = −VH × (D3/2 + D2/4 + D1/8 + D0/16) × (Rf/R)

Here D3 is the most significant bit (MSB), D0 is the least significant bit (LSB), and each bit is either 0 or 1. If Rf = R, the output is negative for a positive logic reference.

Vout = −VH × N/16,   where N = 8D3 + 4D2 + 2D1 + D0

This formula assumes the standard R-2R ladder termination and logic-high reference. The actual output depends on the reference voltage, the exact ladder wiring, and op-amp limits. The supplied screenshot's waveform reaches approximately 4.50 V, but the screenshot does not state the digital reference voltage or individual bit timing.

Resolution and full-scale output

  • Number of input codes: 24 = 16 (0000 through 1111).
  • Ideal LSB step magnitude: |VH|/16 when Rf = R in this convention.
  • Maximum ideal magnitude for 1111: 15|VH|/16.

06 • Simulation procedure

Multisim implementation and verification

  1. Open Multisim and place a 741 op-amp.
  2. Build the R-2R ladder using R = 10 kΩ and 2R = 20 kΩ.
  3. Connect Rf = 10 kΩ from the op-amp output to its inverting input.
  4. Connect the non-inverting input to ground as shown in the circuit.
  5. Connect the op-amp supply pins to +15 V and −15 V.
  6. Provide four digital inputs D3–D0. Use logic levels appropriate for the simulation and common ground.
  7. Change the input code from 0000 to 1111 in binary order.
  8. Observe Vout on the oscilloscope and record the minimum, maximum, and step size.
  9. Compare observed values with the theoretical output for the actual logic-high reference and wiring.

Expected verification table

Digital codeExpected trend
0000Output near zero reference
0001 → 0010 → 0011Output changes by one LSB per increment, ideally
0111 → 1000Carry transition; output increases by one LSB in magnitude
1111Maximum output magnitude, below the reference full-scale by one LSB
07 • Viva voce

Viva questions with answers

1. What is a DAC?

A digital-to-analog converter converts a digital input code into a corresponding analog voltage or current.

2. What does R-2R mean?

It is a resistor ladder network built using only two resistor values, R and 2R.

3. Why is an R-2R ladder preferred?

It needs only two resistor values and is easier to scale to more bits than a binary-weighted resistor network.

4. How many output codes does a 4-bit DAC have?

2⁴ = 16 codes, from 0000 to 1111.

5. What is the MSB?

The most significant bit, which has the largest weight; in this circuit it is D3.

6. What is the LSB?

The least significant bit, which has the smallest weight; in this circuit it is D0.

7. What is resolution?

Resolution is the smallest ideal output change caused by a one-code increment. For this convention with Rf = R, its magnitude is VH/16.

8. What is the role of the op-amp?

It converts the ladder's summed current into an output voltage and provides an active output stage.

9. What is the role of the feedback resistor Rf?

It converts the input current into output voltage and sets the gain factor with the ladder network.

10. Why use 2R resistors?

They establish the ladder's repeated current division and binary weighting.

11. What is full-scale output?

It is the output magnitude at the largest digital input code, 1111.

12. What is monotonicity?

A DAC is monotonic if increasing the input code never causes the output to move in the opposite direction.

13. Why does the output look like a staircase?

The output changes to a new discrete level each time the digital input code changes.

14. Why is the output inverted in this circuit formula?

The op-amp is configured as an inverting current-to-voltage stage, so a positive input current produces a negative output voltage.

15. What is quantization?

Quantization is the representation of a continuous analog range using a finite set of discrete output levels.

16. What errors affect a practical DAC?

Resistor mismatch, reference variation, op-amp offset, finite gain, output swing limits and switching glitches can affect accuracy.

17. Why are ±15 V supplies used for the 741?

They provide positive and negative supply rails so the op-amp can support the required signal range; actual output swing remains limited by the device.

18. What is the purpose of the oscilloscope?

It displays the output voltage over time to show the staircase and measure its range.

09 • Result and conclusion

Observation and conclusion

  • The 4-bit R-2R ladder represents 16 digital input codes.
  • The supplied output screenshot shows a staircase waveform from approximately 0 V to 4.50 V, with Vpp = 4.50 V.
  • The theoretical ideal output depends on the logic-high reference, ladder connections, and op-amp polarity.
Verification note: Your screenshot shows a positive staircase, while the standard inverting formula shown here gives a negative output for a positive reference. This may be due to the specific wiring or signal/reference convention. Confirm the logic-high voltage and connections in Multisim before claiming exact agreement with the theoretical table.

Conclusion: An R-2R ladder DAC converts a 4-bit digital code into a stepped analog output. The circuit screenshot, measured output screenshot, theory, calculations, simulation procedure, viva answers and GATE-style practice questions are included in this webpage.
